headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between Kestra and Slim.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra reads/writes workflow files and logs, and Slim parses Dockerfiles, filesystem artifacts, and interactive CLI input. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pairwise pathway is plausible, not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied artifacts without sanitization, injection becomes reachable.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before handoff.
Review any file-based prompts before execution.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Slim handles filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate private keys, and registry credentials. If they share a workspace or credentials store, sensitive material can flow between them. No isolation boundary is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace, secrets in files may be exposed across the pair.
IF Slim is run on images containing private keys or registry credentials, Kestra can surface them via logs or artifacts.
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts.
Redact secrets from logs before sharing outputs.
Restrict access to credential files.
Rotate any credentials processed by Slim.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and network egress. Kestra can also request root/docker.sock, while Slim requests SYS_ADMIN and privileged mode. In a shared host or directory, concurrent writes and privileged container operations can collide and cause destructive state changes; the overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path, write races can corrupt outputs.
IF both are granted their requested elevated privileges on one host, container and host state can be modified concurrently.
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container or VM.
Assign disjoint output directories.
Disable elevated privileges unless required.
Serialize any shared writes with a lock.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra produces workflow definitions, logs, artifacts, and notifications; Slim is an interactive CLI that can act on container images and registry APIs. If Slim consumes Kestra-generated outputs without verification, a bad workflow or malformed artifact can cascade into incorrect image changes or registry actions. The chain is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Slim is fed Kestra-generated artifacts as authoritative inputs, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Kestra notifications are used as execution triggers, a mistaken workflow can cause repeated actions.
mitigations: Insert a manual review step between agents.
Validate schemas before passing outputs onward.
Require checksums for transferred artifacts.
Limit Slim to dry-run mode where possible.
requires-engineering: add policy gates before any registry or Docker action.

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra handles messages, notifications, cloud storage data, and database data; Slim handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, and vulnerability data. If regulated or secret-bearing data is processed in the same workflow, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both tools, retention and access controls must match.
IF registry credentials or private keys are stored in shared logs, compliance obligations may be breached.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Keep secrets out of shared logs.
Set short retention on workflow artifacts.
Confirm residency for any cloud-stored outputs.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy per agent.
